try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch0.title: Try it yourself: Make the inherited navigation a flex container
try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch0.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The navigation is already spaced and styled, but its layout still depends on normal inline flow. Making nav a flex container gives the parent direct control over how its existing links are arranged. Start from the exact Module 2 checkpoint. Add `nav { display: flex; }` to `styles.css`. Keep every earlier rule and keep the HTML unchanged. Check the navigation: the links should remain together, but the nav is now ready for axis alignment, `gap`, and wrapping decisions.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for make the inherited navigation a flex container so it reinforces Flex Containers and Axes.

try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch1.title: Try it yourself: Stack the existing header content on a vertical main axis
try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch1.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The header contains several pieces of content that should read as one vertical stack. A column flex direction makes that vertical main axis explicit and gives the header a layout model you can align in the next topic. Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `header { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }`. Preview the header: its existing children should stack vertically in a predictable flex flow without new wrappers.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for stack the existing header content on a vertical main axis so it reinforces Flex Containers and Axes.

try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch2.title: Try it yourself: Prepare main content as a column flex container
try_flex_containers_and_axes_sketch2.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

Main contains the content groups that will become the flexible page layout, but it is not yet controlled by Flexbox. Starting main as a column flex container preserves a simple reading order while preparing those existing children for later row and wrap behavior. Keep all previous CSS and add `main { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }`. Do not add wrappers or classes. Check the page: content should remain in a sensible vertical order, now under an explicit flex layout.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for prepare main content as a column flex container so it reinforces Flex Containers and Axes.
